Welcome to Pocket Allowance Ledger — PAL for short. This guide shows you how to use the app day to day.
You use the PAL app on your phone. Your kids use a web page on a Chromebook, tablet, or phone at home — on the same Wi-Fi as your phone.
On your phone you mark jobs done, check balances, and approve what kids send you. On their screen kids see their jobs, tap when finished, and ask for rewards.
This walkthrough uses a sample family named Reyes — kids Maya and Jacob — so you can try the steps right away. When you set up your own family, you choose your own password and each child's PIN.
Along the top, tap a chapter button to jump ahead. Or press play and listen straight through. Previous and Next move one step.
Open PAL. The bottom of the screen has five tabs: Record, Reports, Balances, Approvals, and Contracts.
Record is the Home screen — today's jobs with big Done buttons. That is where most evenings start.
Settings is not a bottom tab. Tap the gear icon to open Settings — kids, kid web, help, and backup live there.
For practice, the sample family password is reyes — all lowercase. The sample PIN for Maya and Jacob is one two three four. When you set up your own family, you pick your own logins.
If your iPhone asks for Local Network permission, tap Allow. That lets the kid web page reach your phone on home Wi-Fi. Keep PAL open while a kid is using that page.
Here is a simple first evening — three steps you will use often.
Step one. On Record, find a job with a Done button. When the job is finished, tap Done. You should see a gold coin, and that child's balance goes up.
Step two. Open Settings with the gear, then tap Kid web. You will see a link and a QR code for the kid page.
On a computer or Chromebook, tap Copy link, then paste the address into the browser. Most PCs cannot scan a QR code.
On a phone or tablet, the child can scan the QR code with the camera if the device supports it. Many iPads can. Same Wi-Fi as your phone either way.
On the kid page, type password reyes, tap Maya, enter PIN one two three four, then tap I did it on a job. That sends you a report. It does not add the coin by itself.
Step three. Back on your phone, open the Approvals tab. Tap Approve to give the tokens, or Decline if the job should not count.
Let's look closer at Record — your main evening screen. Today's jobs appear as large Done buttons.
Each row shows the child's name, the job name, and how many tokens it is worth. You can set different amounts for different jobs.
Tap Done on Maya's morning routine. Watch the coin appear. That means the job was marked done and the tokens were added.
When you tap Done yourself, Balances updates right away. When a kid taps I did it on their page, the tokens wait in Approvals until you say yes.
Sometimes a tip appears on Home after you pay a job less often. It may say things can get bumpier for a little while. Stay steady — you do not need to add extra punishments.
You may also see suggestion cards — for example, paying a job less often once it is going well, or encouraging saving. Read them if you want. Nothing changes unless you agree.
When there are no Done buttons left for today, you are caught up. You can still open any other tab.
Open the Balances tab. Each child shows tokens in hand and tokens banked.
In hand means ready for a sooner reward. Banked means saved toward a bigger goal. Think of two jars for each child.
Tap a child's name to see recent token history and any saving tips for that child.
Wish-list rewards live here too. Kids can ask for them from the kid page. You approve or decline those asks under Approvals.
In the sample, Maya may show more saving tips than Jacob. You can set each child differently when you set up your own family.
Each child's tokens stay with that child.
Kid web is the page kids use. They do not install an app. They open a normal browser on a device that shares your home Wi-Fi.
You stay in the PAL app on your phone. Kids use Chrome, Safari, or another browser on their device. Same home — two screens.
In Settings, open Kid web. When it is ready, the screen says Serving on your network. You will see the kid browser link and a QR code.
For a computer or Chromebook: tap Copy link, open the browser, paste into the address bar, and go.
For a phone or tablet with a camera: open the camera or QR scanner, point at the code, and open the page. Desktops usually cannot do this — use Copy link instead.
Both devices must be on the same home Wi-Fi. If the page will not load, check Wi-Fi, open PAL again on your phone, and retry the link.
If you leave PAL or lock the phone for a long time, the kid page may stop working until you bring PAL back to the front.
Need the link again later? Settings, then Kid web.
On the kid sign-in screen, enter the family password. For the sample, type reyes in lowercase.
Tap the child's name — Maya or Jacob — then enter that child's PIN. Sample PIN is one two three four. Each child only sees their own jobs and tokens.
These sample logins are only for practice. When you set up your own family, you choose your own password and PINs.
Jobs appear as simple tasks. When a child finishes one, they tap I did it. That tells you they are done. The coin still waits for you in Approvals.
After I did it, the kid page usually shows a quick thank-you. On your phone, open Approvals to finish the step.
A child can also ask for a reward from the wish list. That ask appears under Approvals on your phone. Tokens are not spent until you approve.
If two kids share one tablet, sign in with the family password, then each child uses their own name and PIN.
When you are done on the kid page, go back to the Approvals tab on your phone.
Open the Approvals tab. A number on the tab shows how many kid reports are waiting.
Each item shows which child, which job, and when they reported. Read it, then decide.
Tap Approve to add the tokens. Tap Decline if the job should not count — for example if it was not really finished.
Reward asks from the kid page show up here too. Approve spends banked tokens toward that reward. Decline leaves the wish for later.
After you approve, Balances updates. When the kid refreshes their page, they see the new total.
If Approvals is empty, nothing is waiting on you.
Open the Reports tab to see how jobs are going over days and weeks — simple charts and short tips.
Insights can show how often jobs get done, and compare early days with lately.
Trends looks further out. You may see a suggestion to pay a job less often once it is going well.
Tips are optional. If PAL suggests changing a schedule, it asks you first. It will not change schedules by itself.
To save a copy of your data on your phone, use Export backup in Settings — next section.
Open the Contracts tab. This is the list of jobs and routines for each child — what earns tokens and how often.
Tap a job to open its details — how many tokens, how often it pays, and any tips for that job.
A new job can pay often at first, then less often as the habit sticks. Starting amounts follow the child's age as a starting point — you can change them.
If you pay a job less often, you might see a tip that things can get bumpier for a short time. Keep the plan steady through that stretch.
Some jobs include saving reminders. In the sample, Maya may have more of these than Jacob.
Tap New when you want to add a job. Start from a template — morning routine or homework — or make one from scratch.
Enter the name, which child, how many tokens, and how often. Save it. It can then show up on Record with a Done button.
Archive a job when you no longer want it on Record. It stays in history but stops showing Done buttons.
Open Settings with the gear icon. Here you manage kids, kid web, help, and a backup of your data.
Kids list shows each child's profile. Age helps pick starting schedules. You can change those schedules to fit your home.
Kid web is where you copy the link or show the QR so kids can open their page.
Help points to support and this user guide. About shows the app version number.
Export backup saves your jobs, tokens, and settings into a file on your phone. Passwords and PINs are not put in that file.
Use Restore if you move to a new phone and want your household data back.
If PAL wants to change a schedule, it will ask for your confirmation first. It does not change schedules quietly in the background.
You have now seen Record, Balances, kid web, Approvals, Reports, Contracts, and Settings.
To practice the main loop again: tap Done on Record, have a kid tap I did it, then Approve on Approvals.
Use the chapter buttons anytime to jump back to a section.
